ca_6_chronic_wall.blurb: Chronic Wall is the sixth numbered wall at Cecilville Bluffs, a limestone sport cliff in northwest California. It has nine sport routes, all graded, running from 5.10 to 5.12: four in the 5.10s, four in the 5.11s and a single 5.12. The lines are long for a sport crag, and the easier ones are bolted with fairly generous spacing, so expect some distance between clips. It suits climbers building mileage in the 5.10 and 5.11 range. Reaching the wall means following the main trail to the cliff base and then walking along the bottom of the bluffs.

ca_el_gaucho.blurb: El Gaucho is a cliff in the Whitney Portal area above Lone Pine in the Eastern Sierra, set to the right of Roadwork Wall at roughly 8,400 feet. It has nine routes, eight of them trad and one sport, graded from 5.8 to 5.10. Five fall in the 5.10s, with two at 5.9 and two at 5.8, so it is a reasonable stop for climbers working through the middle grades on gear. Some of the easier multi-pitch lines are run-out, which is worth weighing before choosing a route.

ca_fern_grotto.blurb: Fern Grotto is a cluster of blocks in the middle of the Rest Stop Cliffs on Donner Summit, in the Lake Tahoe region at around 7,400 feet. It has nine routes, eight trad and one sport, graded from about 5.7 to 5.10, with three of them in the 5.10 range and most of the rest at 5.8. The bands of rock around it stand under 50 feet, and many routes have anchors reachable from above, which makes the spot workable for top-roping as well as for placing gear.

ca_granny_slab.blurb: Granny Slab is a pyramid-shaped formation, 400 to 500 feet tall, sitting behind Magnus Pillar in the Rock Creek canyon near Mammoth Lakes, at about 9,350 feet. All nine routes are trad: one at 5.7, six in the 5.10s and two in the 5.11s. Many climbs go in several pitches, and neighbouring lines share ledges and anchors, so pitches can be linked. The face leans steeper than it appears from below. It faces southeast, yet stays cooler than the other Rock Creek cliffs because of the elevation and breeze, and in summer shade arrives early in the afternoon.
ca_granny_slab.parking_note: Leave the car at the small paved pullout about 0.4 miles beyond Big Meadow Campground.
ca_granny_slab.approach: Walk across the meadow, cross Rock Creek, then work up and left following cairns, keeping to the right of Juniper Wall and Magnus Pillar. Allow roughly 25 minutes.

ca_hawkins_boulder.blurb: Hawkins Boulder is one of the blocks at The Dreamers, a small bouldering area on the Sherwin Plateau near Mammoth Lakes, at about 7,100 feet. It holds nine problems and the grades stay low: eight at V0 and one V1. Several lines are tall, so pad placement and a good spotter matter near the top. The rock is pocketed tuff. From the parking area, walk down past Crippler Boulder and Hawkins is the next block on the right.

ca_banana_the.blurb: The Banana is one of three boulders in a cluster at Deer Creek Park in Rocklin, in the Sacramento Valley foothills. It has nine problems, from VB up to V4, with most between V0 and V2 and a pair of harder lines at the top end. It sits next to the Monzonite Block and climbs in a similar way, with more easy options. The park is a former quarry with some shade, but Central Valley heat means summer sessions are best kept to mornings.
